One exact CTC toy: the helical Misner quotient

This calculator explores a five-dimensional spacetime that is locally flat but globally identified in a way that can make a continuous route close into its own past. It is a geometric test case for A.R.G.O.'s route solver, not a solved Earth mission.

What this establishes: a continuous timelike loop is mathematically possible in this quotient. What it does not establish: a historical Earth date, a localized drive, a safe ship trajectory, or photons reaching a witness.

Acceleration cost versus onboard duration

For the fixed spatial shift, shortening onboard time pushes the helical orbit toward a null curve and rapidly raises its required proper acceleration.

Model limits: the Misner metric has a compact chronology direction; the helical quotient is global, not a field wall generated around A.R.G.O. Its endpoint is the same manifold event by identification, and T is not an Earth calendar. Matching that event to an ancient Earth observer requires a brane embedding and observer worldline; a sighting then needs a future-directed null ray and an optical source. The route uses propulsion: its fixed-T orbit is timelike but not geodesic.
